prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of flat electronic bands in twisted bilayer graphene at a magic angle and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in that system

statement.case_for: I keep magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene as my preferred configuration after reading the whole first round. The structure is the one the committee should value most: a specific, quantitative prediction in 2011 (Bistritzer and MacDonald) that a continuum model gives nearly flat bands at a discrete twist angle, followed in 2018 by an experiment (Jarillo-Herrero's group) that found correlated insulating and superconducting states at exactly that angle, which nobody expected. That is a discovery, with its origin in a prediction, and it is not an improvement of a known measurement. The consequence is a tunable platform for correlated and topological matter that is now used in many laboratories and has carried over to other moire systems, so the result has already left the group that made it. The citation is now worded to cover the flat-band prediction and the discovery of the correlated and superconducting states, and to say nothing about the pairing mechanism. The chair's question for B030 asks what we would need to see on the origin of the states. I would not make a settled mechanism a precondition: it was not one for the cuprates or for the quantum Hall effects. What I would require is that the experimental phenomenology is robust and reproduced, and I think it is.
statement.case_against: Round 1 sharpened the case against rather than weakened it. Five members (Eriksson, Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson, Pearce) call it early, about eight years after 2018, with an unsettled pairing mechanism and strong sensitivity to twist-angle disorder, and no one else put it in a preferred configuration. Cao, Fatemi and the other first authors, and the Dean, Young, Efetov, Kim, Yazdani and Santos and Lopes dos Santos contributions, are outside the three names, and the three-person limit cannot fix that. B045 and B022 have more settled interpretations and, for B022, a cleaner credit. I also have to admit that a one-member preference is a weak basis for a prize. If the committee thinks that the field needs several more years, then that is a legitimate judgment about timing, and it is not a judgment against the science.

responses.point: Eriksson holds that B045 has a stable interpretation after two decades of materials work, and that B030 should wait until the origin of the correlated states and sensitivity to twist-angle disorder are better understood; he proposes the narrowest defensible quantum spin Hall citation for Kane, Mele and Molenkamp.
responses.response: I agree that B045 is the better-settled case and I did not move it down by much. The narrow citation answers part of what I said in round 1, since a quantum spin Hall and Z2 citation does stand on its own. What still troubles me is that the credit remains incomplete even in the narrow form, because the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal chose HgTe and Zhang cannot be credited. On the maturity point, I still think that the disorder sensitivity concerns the quality of samples and not whether the flat-band-based phenomenology is real. I accept that it counts against waiting being unreasonable, and that is why B045 stays my first alternative.

responses.point: Kroll argues that the lattice-clock architecture, not optical clocks in general, is a discovery-grade invention that is distinct from the 2005 and 2012 prizes, and that a redefinition of the second is not a precondition.
responses.response: This is a better reply to my round-1 objection than I expected. The magic-wavelength lattice that allows many atoms to be interrogated without a light shift is a concrete idea and not simply a tighter version of earlier work, and the narrow citation makes the overlap with the comb and ion-control prizes manageable. I still see it as an invention of an instrument, with the discoveries it will enable mostly still ahead, whereas B030 is a discovery about electrons in a material. I recognise that this is a difference in how I read the statute and not an error in Kroll's argument. I would accept B022, and your Hall-lineage tie, disclosed as it is, does not change my reading of it.

responses.point: Pearce, as chair, treats B030 as a case with merit but too early, and asks me to name what separates it from B022 other than timing; he also says breadth of influence should not decide the prize alone.
responses.response: Fair. Apart from timing, my criterion is that the discovery should sit at the centre of the citation: here a prediction made in advance and a confirming experiment that went beyond it. I agree with you that breadth should not decide alone, and I would rather rest on the specific link between prediction and finding than on the number of groups now working on moire materials. I do not agree that seven or eight years is too short by itself. The 2018 result has been reproduced and extended, and the first-choice case should be judged on reproducibility and not only on the age of the field. If the committee decides that this is early, I would not oppose B022 and would count your two-name case as the clearest attribution on the list.

responses.point: Lindroth says that the microscopic origin of the superconductivity and the correlated states is still disputed after about eight years, and that Cao, Santos and Lopes dos Santos remain outside the credited names, while the clocks have a stable interpretation.
responses.response: I accept the credit point as a real cost. Cao was the first author of the 2018 papers and Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto wrote early flat-band theory, so the trio does not tell the whole story, and I said as much in round 1. My answer is that this applies to every shortlisted ballot, as you also say for the clocks and for B045, and the citation can keep the claim to the prediction at the magic angle and to the discovery of the states. Where we still differ is whether an unsettled mechanism should delay the prize. I think that a stable interpretation of the flat-band origin of the insulators is enough, and I would not delay recognition until the pairing mechanism is settled.

responses.point: Johansson moved to Kane, Mele and Molenkamp for B045, saying that Mele co-authored the Z2 theory and that the 2016 overlap is in the shared theme of topology and not the discovery.
responses.response: This changed my view of B045 a little. I had put the 2016 overlap as a reason for caution, and your distinction between topological phase transitions and Hall conductance on one side and time-reversal-invariant helical edge states on the other is convincing. With Mele in the trio, B045 is a stronger and more coherent configuration than the version I ranked third at the opening, which is why I now put it as my first alternative. It does not move me to prefer it, because the credit story still depends on the HgTe proposal by Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts about eight years after the 2018 experiments as sufficient for a prize while the pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is unsettled.
Whether Cao, Fatemi and other experimental groups, and the early flat-band theorists, can be fairly left out under the three-person limit.

Whether the committee will see the lattice-clock architecture as a discovery or invention under the will, given the 2005 and 2012 prizes; I now regard that as an open question and not a clear objection.
Whether a B045 citation limited to the quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 classification can stand without the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal and the 3D and quantum anomalous Hall strands.
My account of priority and attribution rests on background knowledge and was not independently verified against the supplied files.
statement.conflict_note: No change. No specific conflict is apparent from my profile. My documented connections are David Gross, Hector Rubinstein, Thomas Van Riet and the Uppsala theory group, none of whom is among the credited names on any shortlisted ballot. I note Eriksson's Uppsala materials-theory group as a colleague at my own university in a related area, but I have no documented tie to the credited names on B045 or B030, and I do not propose recusal for any ballot. The Hall-lineage disclosure by Kroll concerns B022 and does not apply to me.
